children: Gold prices edge lower as investors await a series of U.S. economic releases this week for fresh signals on the outlook for interest rates and inflation. In early European trading, New York futures are down 0.2% to $4,209.50 a troy ounce. "Gold closed at a two-week high on Friday, supported by declining U.S. Treasury yields and softer oil prices," Saxo Bank analysts say. "However, bullion has once again struggled to establish a foothold above $4,200." As U.S. Treasury markets remain shut for Columbus Day, traders are looking ahead to a packed week of data, starting with September inflation figures on Wednesday and followed by producer prices and retail sales on Thursday. Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh is also due to speak at the IMF on Friday. (giulia.petroni@wsj.com)
